Daily Devotional

October 4

8 Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. 9 For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. (Colossians 2:8-9 KJV)

Philosophy is a way of thinking. We all have a philosophy, as we all have a way that we think, whether it is a human, worldly way, or a Godly way. The devil is a master at trying to get us to be spoiled by the way we think, and that is what he did to Adam and Eve from the beginning (Genesis 3:1), and he still tries the same thing on us. If the devil can get you to only thinking in a worldly way, and after the tradition of man, then he knows you will not have a Godly philosophy, or way of thinking and living. As the bible says, the way you think in your heart, is how you will be (Proverbs 23:7).

This verse is so awesome, as it says that in Jesus dwells the fullness of the Godhead (Colossians 1:19), and since we are in Jesus (2 Corinthians 5:17), that means that in every born again believer, we have the fullness of God living inside us – WOW! If we Christians could ever just realize what we have in our spirits, we would sure enough become world over comers. We have enough power in our spirits to over come any sickness, disease, financial problem, or anything else the devil or life brings our way, if we would just believe in what God has given us, and by faith release it. This is why Jesus told us, who believe in Him, that we would do the works that He did, and even greater works (John 14:12). Why don’t we just believe that, and go and heal the sick, cast out demons, raise the dead, etc. I think I will just do what Jesus told us to do. Why don’t you also?

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Can we assume this is an upgrade to 16.04 and not a fresh install?

Did you read the discussion around that issue?

I'm not an Ubuntu user, so other people here, feel free to correct me, but from reading that discussion, they mention clearly that Ubuntu since version 15 had replaced their service framework with SystemD. Upstart being the old one.

What you should have done is focus on why the TLP battery service is still trying to use upstart, rather than systemd. Instead you installed the old service framework on an OS with SystemD installed on it and my guess is it has fucked up more services than just TLP from starting, hence the purple screen of doom.

When at the purple screen, press the Esc key. That should show you the boot process and may provide more information about what it is getting stuck at.

My guess is you'll have to drop to the shell (I believe that is Shift + F3), uninstall what you installed and then reinstall/configure SystemD. That link you posted has another link to how you can migrate fully to SystemD.

But hell, I'm still a linux noob, so maybe one of the other guys can give you clearly instructions on how to get out of this mess.

Welcome to Linux, by the way. :)

@Mixplate has the answer.

You replaced systemd with upstart, which while a noble endeavor, is a bit more complex than a simple install script. You'll need to boot the system into single-user mode and either reinstall systemd to get your system back to where it was, or jump through the hoops of fire necessary to get an alternate init system installed -- needless to say, if you're new to Linux, I would suggest sticking with what works out of the box.
